concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: Machines with a finite alphabet, finite states and tapes read and written by heads.

concepts.name: Fixed multitape Turing machine model
concepts.gloss: The bit-complexity model: one deterministic machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, where moving data costs time.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform and convolution
concepts.gloss: The DFT evaluates a sequence at roots of unity; pointwise multiplication of transforms corresponds to convolution of sequences, which is how products are computed.

evidence.quote:

convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.gloss: Splitting each n-bit operand into short radix-2^b digits makes the integer product a convolution of digit lists, followed by carry propagation.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: Placing the digit list on a product of cyclic axes of distinct prime lengths by a Chinese-remainder address map that preserves convolution.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling

concepts.gloss: Keeping the source and target coordinate permutations inside the transform identity so they cancel across the forward and inverse transforms instead of being executed as sorts.

evidence.quote:

concepts.gloss: Rewriting a DFT as a convolution with a chirp (quadratic phase) sequence.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring size
symbols.meaning: A power of two giving the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial of the ring.

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials, satisfying y^r = -1.

concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = -1; multiplying by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote:
one coordinate
is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$
multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.name: Coefficient twist from cyclic to negacyclic
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r} turns cyclic convolution of length r into multiplication modulo y^r+1, with the wrap sign cancelling.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A Nussbaumer-style Fourier transform over the polynomial ring whose roots of unity are powers of y, so multiplications are signed shifts; computed by radix-two butterflies.

evidence.quote:
These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle

concepts.name: Two-point butterfly H₀
concepts.gloss: The map (u,v) ↦ ((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) applied coefficientwise; layers of these make up a radix-two transform.

evidence.quote: H_0(u,v)=\bigl((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2\bigr)

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Multiplying ring polynomials exactly by packing their integer coefficients, including negative ones, into long integers and calling the integer multiplier.

evidence.quote:
The
reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Exact normalized convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Convolution on the remaining axes via forward synthetic transforms, pointwise ring products by signed packing, and the opposite transform consuming the same frequency order.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Tape streams, array order and elementary scans
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in row-major address order on tapes, with linear-time scans, controlled shifts and affine updates of later fields from earlier ones.

evidence.quote: \section{The machine model and elementary streams}

concepts.name: Linear network with roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks of values with signs and restoring auxiliary wires; applied to arrays by giving each wire an invertible frame operator so that intermediate frames cancel and only an endpoint operator remains.

evidence.quote:

concepts.name: Subset-intersection subspace labels
concepts.gloss: Nested subspaces spanned by tensor products of three-element-subset indicator vectors (Frankl–Wilson/Alon style), giving a network whose total edge rank s is less than W·m.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving from rank deficit
concepts.gloss: A call at parameter m·f uses s < W·m calls at parameter f on volume V/W, so normalized cost grows by factor s/W < m per level, giving cost V·(parameter)^{τ} with τ < 1.

evidence.quote:

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address chunks
concepts.title: Fast address interchange at cost $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored bits in the array.

symbols.name: field width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address fields being interchanged.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant below 1 giving the power of u in the cost.

concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layer at cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant below 1 giving the power of d in the cost.

concepts.name: Fixed-point dyadic precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Coefficients stored as p-bit grid values on the unit disk, with truncation errors tracked through contractions so the final integer coefficient error is below 1/2.

evidence.quote:
A single
truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

concepts.name: Fixed rational parameter choice
concepts.gloss: The conservative constants (τ, λ, λ′, ε, δ, κ = 2^{-182}) chosen compatibly so all terms in the cost table fit the main bound.

evidence.quote: These constants are deliberately conservative; no optimization is claimed.

concepts.name: Complete multiplication algorithm and cost
concepts.gloss: Digits → CRT address map → forward synthetic Gaussian-resampled transforms of both operands → pointwise product → inverse transform → rescale, round and carry to get the exact product.

evidence.quote:
The source-transform procedures now supply the three transforms needed
for the radix-digit convolution.

concepts.name: Multiplication in O(n (lg n)^{1-κ}) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: operand length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each input integer.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed positive constant 2^{-182} giving the power saving in the logarithmic factor.

concepts.gloss: The deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplying n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^{1-κ}) time with κ = 2^{-182}, disproving the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: T_A(n)=O\!\left(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}\right),

concepts.name: Linear algebra basics
concepts.gloss: Vectors, matrices, matrix products, invertibility, subspaces, linear independence and rank over the rationals or reals.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo m, including congruence, residues and the fact that coprime moduli behave independently.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Primes, greatest common divisors, coprime integers, and the fact that primes of size about k are plentiful and findable.

concepts.name: Binary representation and radix expansion
concepts.gloss: Writing nonnegative integers as sums of digits times powers of a base, with bit operations such as shifts.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and carries
concepts.gloss: The grade-school algorithm for multiplying integers digit by digit with carries, taking quadratic time.

concepts.name: Divide and conquer and recurrences
concepts.gloss: Solving a problem by splitting it into smaller subproblems and bounding the cost with a recurrence.

concepts.name: Sorting and its cost
concepts.gloss: Rearranging records into a given order, and the n log n cost of doing so.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: Base-2 and natural logarithms and exponentials, including lg n and lg lg n as they appear in running times.

concepts.name: Cartesian product and mixed-radix indexing
concepts.gloss: Indexing an array by tuples of coordinates, one per axis, and flattening to a linear address.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and roots of unity
aliases: additive group of integers mod m
concepts.gloss: The group of residues modulo m under addition, and its use for cyclic indexing and wraparound.

concepts.name: Euclidean norm and unit disk
concepts.gloss: The length of a vector or complex number, the closed disk of modulus at most 1, and the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Fixed-point and rounding arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Representing numbers as integer multiples of a power of 2, rounding to the nearest grid value, and bounding the resulting absolute error.

concepts.name: Proof by induction and summation
concepts.gloss: Standard proof technique and sum formulas used to bound costs level by level in recursion.

concepts.name: Subsets, indicator vectors and set intersection
concepts.gloss: Subsets of a finite set encoded as 0/1 vectors, with sizes counted by binomial coefficients.

concepts.name: Permutation matrices
concepts.gloss: A rearrangement of coordinates represented as a matrix with a single one in each row and column.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and trigonometry
concepts.gloss: The identity e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta, used to write roots of unity and phases.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function exp(-x^2) as a rapidly decaying weight.

concepts.name: Big-endian bit strings and Boolean operations
concepts.gloss: Bit strings and the exclusive-or operation, which is addition modulo 2.

concepts.name: Rational numbers and field arithmetic
concepts.gloss: The rationals as a field closed under addition, multiplication and division by nonzero elements.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: asymptotic analysis, algorithms (including divide and conquer, sorting, and the basic idea of fast multiplication), basic Turing machines, and the supporting mathematics of linear algebra, discrete math, probability-free basics, and complex numbers. They have not studied the FFT in depth, algebraic complexity, polynomial rings modulo relations, number theory beyond modular arithmetic and CRT basics, or numerical error analysis, and they know nothing of the research literature on fast multiplication.
